components.label: Caller
components.responsibility: Own the end-to-end deadline and operation identity.

components.label: Logical request router
components.responsibility: Route calls through a policy that preserves their application contract.

components.label: Eligible round-robin selector
components.responsibility: Choose from an immutable eligible endpoint snapshot; advance the counter atomically.

components.label: Backend pool
components.responsibility: Equivalent application instances own application state through a separate durable store.

components.label: Endpoint directory
components.responsibility: Publish monotonically versioned address and drain snapshots.

components.label: Health sampler
components.responsibility: Combine active probes and passive failures with thresholds and cooldown.

components.label: Deadline and retry budget
components.responsibility: Only retry allowed operations; cap total attempts and remaining deadline.

components.label: Admission controller
components.responsibility: Bound outstanding work and reject overload before a long queue forms.

components.label: Circuit state
components.responsibility: Open on policy thresholds, limit half-open probes, close after successes.

components.label: Drain coordinator
components.responsibility: Withdraw eligibility, keep existing work until deadline, then report forced termination.

components.label: Reverse proxy
components.responsibility: Terminate the request and apply routing policy outside callers.

components.label: Discovery-aware client
components.responsibility: Apply routing inside each controlled caller; keep policy versions observable.

components.label: Unified routing policy
components.responsibility: One owner composes eligibility, admission, deadlines and retry accounting.

requirements.text: Route only to eligible endpoints using an explicit scheduling policy.
Converge on unhealthy endpoints without treating one network timeout as proof of server death.
Bound attempts, deadlines and amplification; preserve application operation identities.
Apply versioned discovery and drain endpoints without terminating accepted work silently.

problem.scope: Route HTTP requests to equivalent backends. The client-discovery approach requires clients we control; neither design retries arbitrary writes safely without an application idempotency contract.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Routing, timeouts, retries and circuit breaking are separate policies.
references.title: Envoy HTTP routing

acceptanceCases.given: Epoch 7 contains A and B; B is not ready.
acceptanceCases.then: Only A receives calls; epoch 6 is ignored.
acceptanceCases.when: Route concurrent calls, then receive stale epoch 6.

acceptanceCases.given: Each operation allows three attempts with a fixed total deadline.
acceptanceCases.then: At most three calls occur; deadline expiry can stop earlier.
acceptanceCases.when: Every backend returns a retryable failure.

acceptanceCases.given: All permits are used and the circuit is open.
acceptanceCases.then: Reject excess calls; permit only a bounded half-open sample; no leak on cancellation.
acceptanceCases.when: A burst arrives and then cooldown ends.

acceptanceCases.given: Endpoint B has accepted work when a newer epoch marks it draining.
acceptanceCases.then: No new B work starts; accepted work completes or gets an explicit deadline outcome.
acceptanceCases.when: Advance the local epoch and finish the accepted work.

guarantees: No unbounded retries; ambiguous write outcomes require idempotency before retry.

assumptions: Backends expose readiness separately from liveness.
Application receipts are durable if write retries are enabled.
solutions.chooseWhen: Heterogeneous clients need one observable routing boundary.

stages.explanation: Begin with a caller and a coarse routing boundary. All attempts belong to one operation ID. [Backpressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_control_%28data%29) prevents producers from outrunning the next component indefinitely. The design must choose whether excess work waits, is rejected, or is dropped with an explicit outcome. Consider this case: Each operation allows three attempts with a fixed total deadline. Every backend returns a retryable failure.
invariants: All attempts belong to one operation ID.
stages.question: Who owns the request deadline?
stages.reason: Begin with a caller and a coarse routing boundary.
stages.title: Draw one request boundary

stages.explanation: Expand the routing boundary into selection and a backend pool. Select against one immutable eligible snapshot. [Backpressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_control_%28data%29) prevents producers from outrunning the next component indefinitely. The design must choose whether excess work waits, is rejected, or is dropped with an explicit outcome. Consider this case: Epoch 7 contains A and B; B is not ready. Route concurrent calls, then receive stale epoch 6.
invariants: Select against one immutable eligible snapshot.
stages.question: How is round robin synchronized?
stages.reason: Expand the routing boundary into selection and a backend pool.
stages.title: Expose selection and destinations

stages.explanation: Make the location of policy an architectural choice, not a label on an arrow. The application contract does not change when routing moves. [Backpressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_control_%28data%29) prevents producers from outrunning the next component indefinitely. The design must choose whether excess work waits, is rejected, or is dropped with an explicit outcome. Consider this case: Epoch 7 contains A and B; B is not ready.
invariants: The application contract does not change when routing moves.
stages.question: Where should routing policy execute?
stages.reason: Make the location of policy an architectural choice, not a label on an arrow.
stages.title: Place a proxy at ingress

stages.explanation: Decouple endpoint membership from request execution. An older discovery epoch cannot replace a newer one. [Replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replication_%28computing%29) keeps copies of state on multiple nodes. Copying data alone does not decide which copy may accept writes or how much stale data a read may return. Consider this case: Endpoint B has accepted work when a newer epoch marks it draining.
invariants: An older discovery epoch cannot replace a newer one.
stages.question: What happens when backends are replaced?
stages.reason: Decouple endpoint membership from request execution.
stages.title: Add versioned endpoint discovery

stages.explanation: Probe and sample failures using explicit thresholds before changing eligibility. A directory entry alone does not imply readiness. [Backpressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_control_%28data%29) prevents producers from outrunning the next component indefinitely. The design must choose whether excess work waits, is rejected, or is dropped with an explicit outcome. Consider this case: Epoch 7 contains A and B; B is not ready.
invariants: A directory entry alone does not imply readiness.
stages.question: Does a timeout prove a backend is dead?
stages.reason: Probe and sample failures using explicit thresholds before changing eligibility.
stages.title: Separate health from membership

stages.explanation: Insert explicit admission and retry accounting before dispatch. Reject when no deadline or permit remains; never create an unbounded retry queue. [Backoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_backoff) spaces repeated attempts so failures do not create a burst of extra traffic. A retry still needs a stable identity and a clear stopping condition. Consider this case: Each operation allows three attempts with a fixed total deadline.
invariants: Reject when no deadline or permit remains; never create an unbounded retry queue.
stages.question: How many backend calls can one caller cause?
stages.reason: Insert explicit admission and retry accounting before dispatch.
stages.title: Bound overload and retry amplification

stages.explanation: Limit half-open probes and coordinate membership removal with accepted work. Draining endpoints receive no new work after the local snapshot advances. [A snapshot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapshot_isolation) gives one read operation a fixed view of data. Later writes may change the live system without changing the rows that reader sees. Consider this case: All permits are used and the circuit is open.
invariants: Draining endpoints receive no new work after the local snapshot advances.
stages.question: How does an endpoint return without another request storm?
stages.reason: Limit half-open probes and coordinate membership removal with accepted work.
stages.title: Add circuit recovery and draining

stages.explanation: Unify policy state while keeping backend execution and discovery separate. Every accepted attempt releases exactly one permit on success, failure or cancellation. [Fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing_%28computing%29) prevents an outdated owner from continuing to modify shared resources. A newer owner needs a token that the resource checks, not merely a belief that ownership changed.
invariants: Every accepted attempt releases exactly one permit on success, failure or cancellation.

operations.reason: One routing state owner must charge attempts and acquire/release permits on every terminal path.

stages.question: Can retry, admission and selection disagree?
stages.reason: Unify policy state while keeping backend execution and discovery separate.
stages.title: Merge policy accounting

solutions.title: Central reverse proxy with bounded routing
tradeoffs: Proxy capacity and availability require independent operation.
An extra hop buys centralized policy and simpler clients.
